A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NGF is not only the "neuronal messenger", which is retrogradly transpo ted to its source, but also the "cytokine", which is produced by target cells, and which modulates the functioning of NGF sensitive cells in a para and/or autocrine manner..

NGF is a "neurotrophin of the second kind" that not only is essential for the development of NGF sensitive neuronal populations but is also a "neuroregulatory" factor that can modulate neuronal function in an autocrine and paracrine fashion in the mature nervous system.
NGF may not be the "magic bullet" for the treatment of neurodegeneration, but rather a "messenger of hope" for the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time course of NGF concentrations in neuropsychiatric disorders is not a mere coincidence.
the time course of NGF changes is a unifying principle for different diseases and may provide a new perspective for the understanding of the aetiology and pathophysiology of these disorders..
